$comment: SHARED. Both the SDK and the App Store implement these rules, so both should
pass this corpus. A case is a complete manifest document plus whether it is
canonically valid; `reason` is a substring the rejection should mention.
The negative cases are mostly package.json SOURCE forms — an author object,
a repository shorthand, a .git suffix, an untrimmed value. They are invalid
on the wire on purpose: a Store that normalized them would be rewriting a
Raw-byte rules — document size, BOM, duplicate member names, nesting depth —
are not expressible here, because a corpus of parsed values has already lost
them. They belong to whoever holds the bytes.

cases.name: the fully populated document is valid
every optional field may be absent
an unknown property is ignored, not rejected
an x- extension is ignored like any other unknown
an unsupported formatVersion is rejected first
a missing formatVersion is rejected
type must be client in v1
entry must be the archive-root remoteEntry.js
a url field is not part of v1 identity but is merely unknown
an id that is not a JavaScript identifier is rejected
a reserved id is rejected
toString is reserved too
an untrimmed id is invalid, not trimmable
build metadata is rejected on the wire
an untrimmed version is invalid, not trimmable
a numeric identifier above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER is rejected
a prerelease within the bound is accepted
an author object is a source form, not a wire form
an author that is an email address is rejected
an untrimmed author is rejected, not trimmed
a present but empty license is rejected — omit it instead
a repository shorthand is a source form
an SSH repository URL is a source form
a .git suffix is a source form
a repository with a query string is rejected
a repositoryDirectory escaping the repository is rejected
a percent escape in repositoryDirectory is rejected
a homepage with credentials is rejected
a non-http homepage scheme is rejected
a local http homepage is accepted on the wire
tags present but empty is rejected — omit it instead
duplicate tags under ASCII case folding are rejected
non-ASCII case differences are two distinct tags
an untrimmed tag is rejected
a non-string tag is rejected
a lone surrogate in any string is rejected
an over-long name is rejected
a manifest that is an array is rejected
a manifest that is a string is rejected
